digest.component_or_area: T11 plan review rubric (post-rollback schema state)
propositions: The T11 post-rollback schema state finding generator produces tautologous advisories (8 of 21 sampled) that clutter signal for append-only stores, drowning rare real catches like data-loss bugs.

Post-rollback findings must be raised only when a plan (a) changes interpretation of existing persisted records, (b) rewrites or migrates records in place, (c) removes or narrows a read path, or (d) performs a one-way transformation with no back-out.

Purely additive, backward-compatible persistence changes (new record/event types, optional fields, new tables/columns with defaults) are explicitly excluded from post-rollback findings because residual data after rollback is normal in append-only and backward-compatible systems.
The applicability rule must not name any persistence store technology so it applies uniformly across SQL migrations, event stores, document databases, and config formats.
